source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֥א יִצְחָ֛ק אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֖ב וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֹת֑וֹ וַיְצַוֵּ֨הוּ֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ לֹֽא־תִקַּ֥ח אִשָּׁ֖ה מִבְּנ֥וֹת כְּנָֽעַן׃

records.literal_gloss: And called Isaac Jacob and blessed him and commanded him and said to him, not you shall take a wife from [the] daughters of Canaan.

en.L: And Isaac called Jacob and blessed him, and commanded him and said to him, "You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan.
en.B: So Isaac sent for Jacob and blessed him, and gave him this charge: "Do not take any Canaanite woman as your wife.
en.R: So Isaac called Jacob to him and blessed him. Then he told him, "Do not marry a woman from the land of Canaan.

es.L: Y llamó Isaac a Jacob y lo bendijo, y le dio una orden y le dijo: «No tomarás mujer de entre las hijas de Canaán.
es.B: Entonces Isaac mandó llamar a Jacob, lo bendijo y le dio este encargo: «No tomes por esposa a ninguna mujer cananea.
es.R: Así que Isaac llamó a Jacob y lo bendijo. Después le dijo: «No te cases con una mujer de la tierra de Canaán.

fr.L: Et Isaac appela Jacob et le bénit, et il lui donna un ordre et lui dit : « Tu ne prendras pas de femme parmi les filles de Canaan.
fr.B: Isaac fit donc venir Jacob, le bénit et lui donna cette consigne : « Ne prends pas pour femme une Cananéenne.
fr.R: Alors Isaac a appelé Jacob et l’a béni. Puis il lui a dit : « N’épouse pas une femme du pays de Canaan.

sw.L: Naye Isaka alimwita Yakobo akambariki, akamwagiza akamwambia, "Usitwae mke katika binti za Kanaani.
sw.B: Basi Isaka alimwita Yakobo, akambariki, akampa agizo hili: "Usioe mwanamke Mkanaani.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Isaka alimwita Yakobo, akambariki. Kisha akamwambia, "Usioe mwanamke wa nchi ya Kanaani.

decisions.choice: blessed him: Isaac now blesses Jacob knowingly
decisions.reason: This time Isaac knows whom he is blessing. He confirms the blessing Jacob took by deceit and adds to it the blessing of Abraham (verses 3-4).

decisions.choice: not from the daughters of Canaan: as Abraham charged his servant
decisions.reason: Abraham made his servant swear not to take a wife for Isaac from the Canaanites, but from his own family (24:3-4). Isaac now gives Jacob the same charge, unlike Esau's marriages (26:34-35; 27:46).

decisions.choice: passé simple for narration at Literal and Balanced ("appela", "bénit"); passé composé at Readable ("a appelé", "a béni")
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets for narrative: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative, the passé composé is how French is spoken and read in school today, which suits Readable.

source.text: ק֥וּם לֵךְ֙ פַּדֶּ֣נָֽה אֲרָ֔ם בֵּ֥יתָה בְתוּאֵ֖ל אֲבִ֣י אִמֶּ֑ךָ וְקַח־לְךָ֤ מִשָּׁם֙ אִשָּׁ֔ה מִבְּנ֥וֹת לָבָ֖ן אֲחִ֥י אִמֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Arise, go to Paddan Aram, [to the] house of Bethuel, [the] father of your mother, and take for yourself from there a wife from [the] daughters of Laban, [the] brother of your mother.

en.L: Arise, go to Paddan-aram, to the house of Bethuel your mother's father, and take a wife for yourself from there, from the daughters of Laban your mother's brother.
en.B: Set out now for Paddan-aram, to the household of your mother's father Bethuel, and find yourself a wife there among the daughters of your uncle Laban.
en.R: Go to Paddan-aram, to the family of Bethuel, your mother's father. Marry one of the daughters of your mother's brother Laban.

es.L: Levántate, ve a Padán Aram, a la casa de Betuel, el padre de tu madre, y toma para ti de allí mujer de entre las hijas de Labán, el hermano de tu madre.
es.B: Ponte ahora en camino hacia Padán Aram, a la casa de Betuel, el padre de tu madre, y busca allí esposa entre las hijas de tu tío Labán.
es.R: Ve a Padán Aram, a la familia de Betuel, el padre de tu madre. Cásate con una de las hijas de Labán, el hermano de tu madre.

fr.L: Lève-toi, va à Paddân-Aram, à la maison de Béthuel, le père de ta mère, et prends-toi de là une femme parmi les filles de Laban, le frère de ta mère.
fr.B: Pars maintenant pour Paddân-Aram, chez Béthuel, le père de ta mère, et choisis-y une femme parmi les filles de ton oncle Laban.
fr.R: Va à Paddân-Aram, dans la famille de Béthuel, le père de ta mère. Épouse une des filles de Laban, le frère de ta mère.

sw.L: Ondoka, nenda Padan-aramu, kwenye nyumba ya Bethueli baba wa mama yako, ujitwalie mke kutoka huko katika binti za Labani, ndugu wa mama yako.
sw.B: Ondoka sasa uende Padan-aramu, nyumbani kwa Bethueli, baba wa mama yako, ukajitafutie mke huko miongoni mwa binti za mjomba wako Labani.
sw.R: Nenda Padan-aramu, kwa jamaa ya Bethueli, baba wa mama yako. Umwoe mmoja wa binti za Labani, kaka wa mama yako.

decisions.choice: Paddan-aram: the region of Haran in upper Mesopotamia
decisions.reason: The name probably means "the field" or "plain of Aram". It is the area around Haran (27:43; 29:4), on the upper Euphrates, where Abraham's brother Nahor's family lived (24:10).

decisions.choice: a wife from the daughters of Laban: marriage within the wider family
decisions.reason: Marrying a cousin kept the family line and its faith together. Isaac married Rebekah, the granddaughter of his father's brother (24:15).

decisions.choice: "mjomba wako Labani"
decisions.reason: Swahili has a word for a mother's brother, "mjomba", which says exactly what the English "your uncle" says without the ambiguity of English "uncle".

source.text: וְאֵ֤ל שַׁדַּי֙ יְבָרֵ֣ךְ אֹֽתְךָ֔ וְיַפְרְךָ֖ וְיַרְבֶּ֑ךָ וְהָיִ֖יתָ לִקְהַ֥ל עַמִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And God Almighty may he bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you, and you will become an assembly of peoples.

en.L: And may God Almighty bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you, so that you become an assembly of peoples.
en.B: May God Almighty bless you, give you children and make them many, until you grow into a whole gathering of peoples.
en.R: May God Almighty bless you. May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} give you many children, so that your family grows into many peoples.

es.L: Y el Dios Todopoderoso te bendiga y te haga fecundo y te multiplique, y llegarás a ser una congregación de pueblos.
es.B: Que el Dios Todopoderoso te bendiga, te dé hijos y los multiplique, hasta que llegues a ser toda una asamblea de pueblos.
es.R: Que el Dios Todopoderoso te bendiga. Que te dé muchos hijos, para que tu familia llegue a ser muchos pueblos.

fr.L: Et que le Dieu tout-puissant te bénisse, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te rende fécond et te multiplie, et tu deviendras une assemblée de peuples.
fr.B: Que le Dieu tout-puissant te bénisse, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te donne des enfants et les rende nombreux, jusqu’à ce que tu deviennes toute une assemblée de peuples.
fr.R: Que le Dieu tout-puissant te bénisse. Qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te donne beaucoup d’enfants, pour que ta famille devienne de nombreux peuples.

sw.L: Na Mungu Mwenyezi akubariki, akuzalishe na akuongeze, nawe uwe kusanyiko la mataifa.
sw.B: Mungu Mwenyezi akubariki, akupe watoto na kuwazidisha, mpaka uwe kusanyiko zima la mataifa.
sw.R: Mungu Mwenyezi akubariki. Akupe watoto wengi, ili jamaa yako ikue kuwa mataifa mengi.

decisions.choice: God Almighty (El Shaddai): the name God gave when he made his covenant with Abraham
decisions.reason: God named himself El Shaddai when he promised Abraham many descendants (17:1-2). Isaac calls on that name as he passes the promise to Jacob, and God uses it again to Jacob himself (35:11).

decisions.choice: fruitful and multiply: the first blessing on humankind
decisions.reason: The words recall God's blessing at creation and after the flood (1:28; 9:1), and God's promise to Abraham (17:2, 6).

decisions.choice: an assembly of peoples (qehal ammim): a great gathered company
decisions.reason: Qahal is a gathering or assembly, later used of Israel gathered before God. Jacob's twelve sons will become the tribes of one people (35:11; 48:4).

decisions.choice: May he give you
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to God, so it takes the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: "qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te rende fécond" (L), "qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te donne" (B)
alternatives: no span, as the English Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: French repeats the subject pronoun for God in the second wish where English does not, so the deity pronoun setting appears at Literal and Balanced too.

source.text: וְיִֽתֶּן־לְךָ֙ אֶת־בִּרְכַּ֣ת אַבְרָהָ֔ם לְךָ֖ וּלְזַרְעֲךָ֣ אִתָּ֑ךְ לְרִשְׁתְּךָ֙ אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ מְגֻרֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְאַבְרָהָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And may he give to you [the] blessing of Abraham, to you and to your offspring with you, to possess [the] land of your sojournings, which gave God to Abraham.

en.L: And may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} give you the blessing of Abraham, to you and to your offspring with you, that you may take possession of the land of your sojournings, which God gave to Abraham."
en.B: May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} give you and your descendants the blessing {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave Abraham, so that you will possess the land where you now live as a foreigner, the land God gave to Abraham."
en.R: May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} give you and your descendants the blessing {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave to Abraham. Then you will own this land where you now live as a foreigner. God gave this land to Abraham."

es.L: Y te dé la bendición de Abraham, a ti y a tu descendencia contigo, para que poseas la tierra de tus peregrinaciones, la que Dios dio a Abraham».
es.B: Que te dé a ti y a tus descendientes la bendición que le dio a Abraham, para que poseas la tierra donde ahora vives como extranjero, la tierra que Dios le dio a Abraham».
es.R: Que te dé a ti y a tus descendientes la bendición que le dio a Abraham. Así serás dueño de esta tierra donde ahora vives como extranjero. Dios le dio esta tierra a Abraham».

fr.L: Et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te donne la bénédiction d’Abraham, à toi et à ta descendance avec toi, pour que tu prennes possession du pays de tes séjours, que Dieu a donné à Abraham. »
fr.B: Qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous donne, à toi et à tes descendants, la bénédiction qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a donnée à Abraham, afin que tu possèdes le pays où tu vis maintenant en étranger, le pays que Dieu a donné à Abraham. »
fr.R: Qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te donne, à toi et à tes descendants, la bénédiction qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a donnée à Abraham. Alors ce pays où tu vis maintenant comme étranger sera à toi. Dieu l’a donné à Abraham. »

sw.L: Na akupe baraka ya Abrahamu, wewe na uzao wako pamoja nawe, ili uimiliki nchi ya ugeni wako, ambayo Mungu alimpa Abrahamu."
sw.B: Akupe wewe na wazao wako baraka aliyompa Abrahamu, ili uimiliki nchi unamoishi sasa kama mgeni, nchi ambayo Mungu alimpa Abrahamu."
sw.R: Akupe wewe na wazao wako baraka aliyompa Abrahamu. Ndipo utakapoimiliki nchi hii unamoishi sasa kama mgeni. Mungu alimpa Abrahamu nchi hii."

decisions.choice: the blessing of Abraham: the promises God made to Abraham
decisions.reason: Land, descendants and blessing for the nations (12:2-3; 17:8). Isaac passes them on to Jacob, not Esau; God confirms it at Bethel (verses 13-14).

decisions.choice: the land of your sojournings: where you live as a resident foreigner
decisions.reason: The patriarchs lived in Canaan without owning it, except for a burial place (23:4, 17-20). The promise is that their descendants will possess it.

decisions.choice: offspring (L), descendants (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in earlier chapters, zera is "offspring" at Literal and "descendants" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: he (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: The "he" who gives the blessing is God (verse 3), so the pronoun takes the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: no deity pronoun span ("Que te dé")
decisions.reason: Spanish leaves the subject in the verb, so there is no pronoun for the English "he" span to sit on; adding "él" would only be there to carry the setting.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יִצְחָק֙ אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹ֔ב וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ פַּדֶּ֣נָֽה אֲרָ֑ם אֶל־לָבָ֤ן בֶּן־בְּתוּאֵל֙ הָֽאֲרַמִּ֔י אֲחִ֣י רִבְקָ֔ה אֵ֥ם יַעֲקֹ֖ב וְעֵשָֽׂו׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent away Isaac Jacob, and he went to Paddan Aram, to Laban, son of Bethuel the Aramean, [the] brother of Rebekah, [the] mother of Jacob and Esau.

en.L: And Isaac sent Jacob away, and he went to Paddan-aram, to Laban the son of Bethuel the Aramean, the brother of Rebekah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.
en.B: Then Isaac sent Jacob on his way, and he set out for Paddan-aram, to Laban son of Bethuel the Aramean. Laban was the brother of Rebekah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.
en.R: Then Isaac sent Jacob away. Jacob went to Paddan-aram, to Laban. Laban was the son of Bethuel the Aramean and the brother of Rebekah, Jacob and Esau's mother.

es.L: Y despidió Isaac a Jacob, y él fue a Padán Aram, a Labán, hijo de Betuel el arameo, hermano de Rebeca, la madre de Jacob y de Esaú.
es.B: Entonces Isaac despidió a Jacob, y este se dirigió a Padán Aram, a casa de Labán, hijo de Betuel el arameo. Labán era hermano de Rebeca, la madre de Jacob y de Esaú.
es.R: Después Isaac despidió a Jacob. Jacob fue a Padán Aram, a casa de Labán. Labán era hijo de Betuel el arameo y hermano de Rebeca, la madre de Jacob y Esaú.

fr.L: Et Isaac renvoya Jacob, et il alla à Paddân-Aram, chez Laban, fils de Béthuel l’Araméen, frère de Rébecca, la mère de Jacob et d’Ésaü.
fr.B: Puis Isaac fit partir Jacob, qui se mit en route pour Paddân-Aram, chez Laban, fils de Béthuel l’Araméen. Laban était le frère de Rébecca, la mère de Jacob et d’Ésaü.
fr.R: Ensuite Isaac a fait partir Jacob. Jacob est allé à Paddân-Aram, chez Laban. Laban était le fils de Béthuel l’Araméen et le frère de Rébecca, la mère de Jacob et d’Ésaü.

sw.L: Naye Isaka akamwacha Yakobo aende, naye akaenda Padan-aramu kwa Labani mwana wa Bethueli Mwaramu, ndugu wa Rebeka, mama wa Yakobo na Esau.
sw.B: Kisha Isaka akamruhusu Yakobo aende zake, naye akashika njia kwenda Padan-aramu, kwa Labani mwana wa Bethueli Mwaramu. Labani alikuwa kaka wa Rebeka, mama wa Yakobo na Esau.
sw.R: Kisha Isaka akamuaga Yakobo. Yakobo akaenda Padan-aramu, kwa Labani. Labani alikuwa mwana wa Bethueli Mwaramu, na kaka wa Rebeka, mama wa Yakobo na Esau.

decisions.choice: the Aramean: of the people of Aram
decisions.reason: Arameans lived in the region of Haran and later in Syria. Israel later remembered its ancestor as "a wandering Aramean" (Deuteronomy 26:5).

decisions.choice: the mother of Jacob and Esau: Jacob named first
decisions.reason: The younger son is named before the older, as he has now received the blessing of the firstborn.

source.text: וַיַּ֣רְא עֵשָׂ֗ו כִּֽי־בֵרַ֣ךְ יִצְחָק֮ אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹב֒ וְשִׁלַּ֤ח אֹתוֹ֙ פַּדֶּ֣נָֽה אֲרָ֔ם לָקַֽחַת־ל֥וֹ מִשָּׁ֖ם אִשָּׁ֑ה בְּבָרֲכ֣וֹ אֹת֔וֹ וַיְצַ֤ו עָלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹֽא־תִקַּ֥ח אִשָּׁ֖ה מִבְּנ֥וֹת כְּנָֽעַן׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw Esau that had blessed Isaac Jacob and sent him to Paddan Aram to take for himself from there a wife, when he blessed him, and he commanded him, saying, not you shall take a wife from [the] daughters of Canaan,

en.L: And Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him away to Paddan-aram to take a wife for himself from there, and that as he blessed him he commanded him, saying, "You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan,"
en.B: Esau learned that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him to Paddan-aram to find a wife there, and that when he blessed him he had told him, "Do not marry a Canaanite woman,"
en.R: Esau learned that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him to Paddan-aram to find a wife there. He heard that Isaac had told Jacob, "Do not marry a woman from Canaan."

es.L: Y vio Esaú que Isaac había bendecido a Jacob y lo había enviado a Padán Aram para tomar de allí mujer para sí, y que al bendecirlo le había mandado diciendo: «No tomarás mujer de entre las hijas de Canaán»,
es.B: Esaú se enteró de que Isaac había bendecido a Jacob y lo había enviado a Padán Aram para buscar allí esposa, y de que al bendecirlo le había dicho: «No te cases con una cananea»,
es.R: Esaú supo que Isaac había bendecido a Jacob y lo había enviado a Padán Aram a buscar esposa. Oyó que Isaac le había dicho a Jacob: «No te cases con una mujer de Canaán».

fr.L: Et Ésaü vit qu’Isaac avait béni Jacob et l’avait envoyé à Paddân-Aram pour y prendre une femme, et qu’en le bénissant il lui avait donné cet ordre : « Tu ne prendras pas de femme parmi les filles de Canaan »,
fr.B: Ésaü apprit qu’Isaac avait béni Jacob et l’avait envoyé à Paddân-Aram pour y trouver une femme, et qu’en le bénissant il lui avait dit : « N’épouse pas une Cananéenne »,
fr.R: Ésaü a appris qu’Isaac avait béni Jacob et l’avait envoyé à Paddân-Aram pour y trouver une femme. On lui a dit qu’Isaac avait ordonné à Jacob : « N’épouse pas une femme de Canaan. »

sw.L: Naye Esau aliona ya kwamba Isaka amembariki Yakobo na kumpeleka Padan-aramu ajitwalie mke kutoka huko, na ya kwamba alipombariki alimwagiza, akisema, "Usitwae mke katika binti za Kanaani,"
sw.B: Esau alipata habari kwamba Isaka amembariki Yakobo na kumpeleka Padan-aramu ili akatafute mke huko, na kwamba alipombariki alimwambia, "Usioe mwanamke Mkanaani,"
sw.R: Esau alisikia kwamba Isaka amembariki Yakobo na kumpeleka Padan-aramu akatafute mke huko. Alisikia kwamba Isaka alimwambia Yakobo, "Usioe mwanamke wa Kanaani."

decisions.choice: Esau saw: the start of a long sentence (verses 6-9)
decisions.reason: Esau sees three things (verses 6-8), and acts on them in verse 9.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע יַעֲקֹ֔ב אֶל־אָבִ֖יו וְאֶל־אִמּ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ פַּדֶּ֥נָֽה אֲרָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and listened Jacob to his father and to his mother and went to Paddan Aram.

en.L: and that Jacob had listened to his father and his mother and gone to Paddan-aram.
en.B: and that Jacob had done what his father and mother told him and gone to Paddan-aram.
en.R: He also learned that Jacob had obeyed his father and mother and gone to Paddan-aram.

es.L: y que Jacob había escuchado a su padre y a su madre y se había ido a Padán Aram.
es.B: y que Jacob había hecho lo que le dijeron su padre y su madre, y se había ido a Padán Aram.
es.R: También supo que Jacob había obedecido a su padre y a su madre y se había ido a Padán Aram.

fr.L: et que Jacob avait écouté son père et sa mère et était allé à Paddân-Aram.
fr.B: et que Jacob avait fait ce que son père et sa mère lui avaient dit, et était parti pour Paddân-Aram.
fr.R: Il a aussi appris que Jacob avait obéi à son père et à sa mère et qu’il était parti à Paddân-Aram.

sw.L: na ya kwamba Yakobo alikuwa amemsikiliza baba yake na mama yake, akaenda Padan-aramu.
sw.B: na kwamba Yakobo alikuwa amefanya kama baba yake na mama yake walivyomwambia, akaenda Padan-aramu.
sw.R: Alisikia pia kwamba Yakobo aliwatii baba yake na mama yake, akaenda Padan-aramu.

decisions.choice: listened to his father and his mother: obeyed them
decisions.reason: To "listen to" someone is to obey them. The contrast is with Esau, who married against his parents' wishes (26:34-35).

source.text: וַיַּ֣רְא עֵשָׂ֔ו כִּ֥י רָע֖וֹת בְּנ֣וֹת כְּנָ֑עַן בְּעֵינֵ֖י יִצְחָ֥ק אָבִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw Esau that [were] evil [the] daughters of Canaan in [the] eyes of Isaac his father.

en.L: And Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan were displeasing in the eyes of Isaac his father.
en.B: It was clear to Esau, then, that his father Isaac did not approve of Canaanite women,
en.R: Esau now understood that his father Isaac did not like the women of Canaan.

es.L: Y vio Esaú que las hijas de Canaán eran malas a los ojos de Isaac su padre.
es.B: Así Esaú vio con claridad que a su padre Isaac no le agradaban las mujeres cananeas,
es.R: Esaú entendió entonces que a su padre Isaac no le gustaban las mujeres de Canaán.

fr.L: Et Ésaü vit que les filles de Canaan étaient mauvaises aux yeux d’Isaac, son père.
fr.B: Ésaü comprit alors que son père Isaac voyait d’un mauvais œil les femmes cananéennes,
fr.R: Ésaü a compris alors que son père Isaac n’aimait pas les femmes de Canaan.

sw.L: Naye Esau akaona ya kwamba binti za Kanaani walikuwa wabaya machoni pa Isaka baba yake.
sw.B: Ndipo Esau akatambua kwamba baba yake Isaka hapendezwi na wanawake Wakanaani,
sw.R: Sasa Esau akaelewa kwamba baba yake Isaka hawapendi wanawake wa Kanaani.

decisions.choice: evil in the eyes of: displeasing to
decisions.reason: "Evil in someone's eyes" means that the person dislikes or disapproves of something.

source.text: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ עֵשָׂ֖ו אֶל־יִשְׁמָעֵ֑אל וַיִּקַּ֡ח אֶֽת־מָחֲלַ֣ת׀בַּת־יִשְׁמָעֵ֨אל בֶּן־אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֲח֧וֹת נְבָי֛וֹת עַל־נָשָׁ֖יו ל֥וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And went Esau to Ishmael and took Mahalath, daughter of Ishmael, son of Abraham, [the] sister of Nebaioth, in addition to his wives, for himself as a wife.

en.L: And Esau went to Ishmael and took Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham's son, the sister of Nebaioth, as his wife, in addition to the wives he had.
en.B: so he went to Ishmael's family and, besides the wives he already had, took as his wife Mahalath, the daughter of Abraham's son Ishmael and sister of Nebaioth.
en.R: So Esau went to the family of Ishmael, Abraham's son. He married Ishmael's daughter Mahalath, the sister of Nebaioth. He already had other wives.

es.L: Y se fue Esaú a Ismael y tomó por mujer a Majalat, hija de Ismael hijo de Abraham, hermana de Nebayot, además de las mujeres que tenía.
es.B: así que fue a la familia de Ismael y, además de las mujeres que ya tenía, tomó por esposa a Majalat, hija de Ismael, el hijo de Abraham, y hermana de Nebayot.
es.R: Por eso Esaú fue a la familia de Ismael, el hijo de Abraham. Se casó con Majalat, la hija de Ismael y hermana de Nebayot. Esaú ya tenía otras esposas.

fr.L: Et Ésaü alla vers Ismaël, et il prit Mahalath, fille d’Ismaël, fils d’Abraham, sœur de Nebayoth, pour femme, en plus des femmes qu’il avait.
fr.B: il alla donc dans la famille d’Ismaël et, en plus des femmes qu’il avait déjà, il épousa Mahalath, fille d’Ismaël, fils d’Abraham, et sœur de Nebayoth.
fr.R: Alors Ésaü est allé dans la famille d’Ismaël, le fils d’Abraham. Il a épousé Mahalath, la fille d’Ismaël et la sœur de Nebayoth. Il avait déjà d’autres femmes.

sw.L: Naye Esau akaenda kwa Ishmaeli, akamtwaa Mahalathi binti Ishmaeli mwana wa Abrahamu, dada wa Nebayothi, kuwa mke wake, zaidi ya wake aliokuwa nao.
sw.B: basi akaenda kwa jamaa ya Ishmaeli, na zaidi ya wake aliokuwa nao tayari, akamwoa Mahalathi, binti wa Ishmaeli mwana wa Abrahamu, dada yake Nebayothi.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Esau akaenda kwa jamaa ya Ishmaeli, mwana wa Abrahamu. Akamwoa Mahalathi, binti wa Ishmaeli, dada yake Nebayothi. Esau alikuwa tayari na wake wengine.

decisions.choice: went to Ishmael: to Ishmael's family
decisions.reason: Ishmael had probably already died (25:17), so this means his people. Nebaioth was Ishmael's firstborn (25:13), who would have been head of the family.

decisions.choice: Mahalath: called Basemath in 36:3
decisions.reason: The list of Esau's wives in 36:3 calls Ishmael's daughter Basemath. Women sometimes bore more than one name; the Hebrew of each passage is followed as it stands.

decisions.choice: in addition to the wives he had: Esau tries to please, but late
decisions.reason: Esau marries into Abraham's family to please his father, but he keeps his Hittite wives, and Ishmael's line is not the line of the promise (17:19-21).

decisions.choice: Ishmael's family (B); the family of Ishmael (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "to Ishmael" (m1).

source.text: וַיֵּצֵ֥א יַעֲקֹ֖ב מִבְּאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ חָרָֽנָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out Jacob from Beersheba and went to Haran.

en.L: And Jacob went out from Beersheba and went toward Haran.
en.B: Jacob left Beersheba and set out for Haran.
en.R: Jacob left Beersheba and started on his way to Haran.

es.L: Y salió Jacob de Beerseba y fue hacia Harán.
es.B: Jacob dejó Beerseba y partió hacia Harán.
es.R: Jacob salió de Beerseba y se puso en camino a Harán.

fr.L: Et Jacob sortit de Beer-Shéba et alla vers Harân.
fr.B: Jacob quitta Beer-Shéba et partit pour Harân.
fr.R: Jacob a quitté Beer-Shéba et il s’est mis en route vers Harân.

sw.L: Yakobo alitoka Beer-sheba, akaenda kuelekea Harani.
sw.B: Yakobo aliondoka Beer-sheba, akashika njia kwenda Harani.
sw.R: Yakobo aliondoka Beer-sheba, akaanza safari ya kwenda Harani.

decisions.choice: from Beersheba toward Haran: a journey of several hundred miles
decisions.reason: Beersheba was in the far south of Canaan (26:23-33); Haran was in upper Mesopotamia, some 500 miles (800 km) away to the northeast. Jacob travels alone, unlike Abraham's servant with his ten camels (24:10).

decisions.choice: toward (L); set out for (B); started on his way to (R)
decisions.reason: The verse tells where Jacob was heading; the journey is told in what follows (29:1-4).

source.text: וַיִּפְגַּ֨ע בַּמָּק֜וֹם וַיָּ֤לֶן שָׁם֙ כִּי־בָ֣א הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ וַיִּקַּח֙ מֵאַבְנֵ֣י הַמָּק֔וֹם וַיָּ֖שֶׂם מְרַֽאֲשֹׁתָ֑יו וַיִּשְׁכַּ֖ב בַּמָּק֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And he came upon the place and spent the night there, for had set the sun; and he took from [the] stones of the place and put [it at] his head, and lay down in that place.

en.L: And he came upon a certain place and spent the night there, because the sun had set. And he took one of the stones of the place and put [it at] his head, and lay down in that place.
en.B: He came to a certain place and stopped there for the night, because the sun had gone down. Taking one of the stones from there, he put it by his head and lay down to sleep in that place.
en.R: When the sun went down, Jacob came to a place where he stopped for the night. He took one of the stones there and put it by his head. Then he lay down to sleep.

es.L: Y llegó a un lugar y pasó la noche allí, porque el sol se había puesto. Y tomó una de las piedras del lugar y [la] puso junto a su cabeza, y se acostó en aquel lugar.
es.B: Llegó a cierto lugar y se detuvo allí para pasar la noche, porque el sol ya se había ocultado. Tomó una de las piedras del lugar, la colocó junto a su cabeza y se acostó a dormir allí.
es.R: Cuando se puso el sol, Jacob llegó a un lugar donde se quedó a pasar la noche. Tomó una de las piedras que había allí y la puso junto a su cabeza. Luego se acostó a dormir.

fr.L: Et il arriva en un lieu et y passa la nuit, car le soleil s’était couché. Et il prit une des pierres du lieu et [la] mit à son chevet, et il se coucha en ce lieu.
fr.B: Il arriva en un certain lieu et s’y arrêta pour la nuit, car le soleil s’était couché. Il prit une des pierres du lieu, la plaça près de sa tête et se coucha là pour dormir.
fr.R: Quand le soleil s’est couché, Jacob est arrivé à un endroit où il s’est arrêté pour la nuit. Il a pris une des pierres qui étaient là et l’a mise près de sa tête. Puis il s’est couché pour dormir.

sw.L: Akafika mahali fulani akakaa huko usiku kucha, kwa kuwa jua lilikuwa limetua. Akachukua jiwe moja kati ya mawe ya mahali hapo, akaliweka penye kichwa chake, akajilaza mahali hapo.
sw.B: Alifika mahali fulani, akasimama hapo kulala usiku, kwa sababu jua lilikuwa limetua. Akachukua jiwe moja la mahali hapo, akaliweka karibu na kichwa chake, akajilaza pale ili alale.
sw.R: Jua lilipotua, Yakobo alifika mahali fulani, akaamua kulala hapo usiku. Akachukua jiwe moja lililokuwa pale, akaliweka karibu na kichwa chake. Kisha akalala.

decisions.choice: the place (hammaqom): a place that will prove holy
decisions.reason: "The place" is named three times in this verse and again in verses 16-17 and 19. The word is often used of a holy site (12:6; 22:3-4). At first it is just somewhere to stop; by morning it is the house of God.

decisions.choice: at his head: beside or under his head
decisions.reason: The word (mera'ashot) means the place at the head. The stone may have served as a headrest or as protection beside his head.

decisions.choice: [it at]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the words the Hebrew leaves understood.

source.text: וַֽיַּחֲלֹ֗ם וְהִנֵּ֤ה סֻלָּם֙ מֻצָּ֣ב אַ֔רְצָה וְרֹאשׁ֖וֹ מַגִּ֣יעַ הַשָּׁמָ֑יְמָה וְהִנֵּה֙ מַלְאֲכֵ֣י אֱלֹהִ֔ים עֹלִ֥ים וְיֹרְדִ֖ים בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he dreamed, and look, a stairway [was] set on [the] earth, and its top [was] reaching [to] the heavens; and look, [the] angels of God [were] going up and going down on it.

en.L: And he dreamed, and look, a stairway was set up on the earth, and its top reached to the heavens; and look, the angels of God were going up and going down on it.
en.B: He dreamed, and there before him was a stairway standing on the ground, its top touching the sky, with God's angels climbing up and coming down on it.
en.R: Jacob had a dream. He saw a stairway standing on the earth. Its top reached up into the sky. God's angels were going up and coming down the stairway.

es.L: Y tuvo un sueño, y he aquí, una escalera colocada sobre la tierra, cuya cima alcanzaba hasta los cielos; y he aquí, los ángeles de Dios iban subiendo y bajando por ella.
es.B: Soñó, y vio ante sí una escalera plantada en el suelo, con la parte alta tocando el cielo, y por ella subían y bajaban los ángeles de Dios.
es.R: Jacob tuvo un sueño. Vio una escalera que estaba sobre la tierra. La parte de arriba llegaba hasta el cielo. Los ángeles de Dios subían y bajaban por la escalera.

fr.L: Et il rêva, et voici, un escalier était dressé sur la terre, et son sommet atteignait les cieux ; et voici, des anges de Dieu y montaient et descendaient.
fr.B: Il eut un rêve : un escalier se dressait là, posé sur le sol, et son sommet touchait le ciel ; des anges de Dieu y montaient et en descendaient.
fr.R: Jacob a fait un rêve. Il a vu un escalier posé sur la terre. Le haut de l’escalier arrivait jusqu’au ciel. Des anges de Dieu montaient et descendaient sur cet escalier.

sw.L: Naye akaota, na tazama, ngazi ilikuwa imewekwa juu ya ardhi, na kilele chake kilifikia mbingu; na tazama, malaika wa Mungu walikuwa wakipanda na kuteremka kwa ngazi hiyo.
sw.B: Aliota ndoto, akaona mbele yake ngazi imesimama ardhini, kilele chake kikigusa anga, na malaika wa Mungu wakipanda na kuteremka juu yake.
sw.R: Yakobo aliota ndoto. Aliona ngazi iliyosimama juu ya ardhi. Ncha yake ya juu ilifika mpaka angani. Malaika wa Mungu walikuwa wakipanda na kushuka kwenye ngazi hiyo.

decisions.choice: a stairway (sullam): a staircase or ramp
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. It comes from a root meaning to heap up, and suggests a ramp or a flight of steps, like the stairs of the stepped temple towers of Mesopotamia, rather than a ladder. The familiar rendering "ladder" is not wrong, but people do not usually go up and down a ladder side by side.

decisions.choice: angels of God going up and down: heaven and earth joined
decisions.reason: Jacob sees that the place is linked to heaven (verse 17). Jesus takes up the picture of himself: "you will see heaven opened, and the angels of God going up and coming down on the Son of Man" (John 1:51).

decisions.choice: and look ... and look: the dreamer's view
decisions.reason: Hinneh, three times in verses 12-13, lets the reader see the dream through Jacob's eyes.

decisions.choice: "un escalier"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads sullam as a stairway or ramp rather than a ladder. Spanish "escalera" and Swahili "ngazi" cover both, but French must choose, and "échelle" is only a ladder.

source.text: וְהִנֵּ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה נִצָּ֣ב עָלָיו֮ וַיֹּאמַר֒ אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה אֱלֹהֵי֙ אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֔יךָ וֵאלֹהֵ֖י יִצְחָ֑ק הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתָּה֙ שֹׁכֵ֣ב עָלֶ֔יהָ לְךָ֥ אֶתְּנֶ֖נָּה וּלְזַרְעֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And look, YHWH [was] standing above it and said, I [am] YHWH, [the] God of Abraham your father and [the] God of Isaac; the land which you [are] lying on it, to you I will give it and to your offspring.

en.L: And look, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stood above it and said, "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac. The land on which you are lying I will give to you and to your offspring.
en.B: There above it stood {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your father Abraham and of Isaac. To you and to your descendants I will give the ground you are lying on.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was standing above the stairway. He said, "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your grandfather Abraham and the God of your father Isaac. I will give you and your descendants this land you are lying on.

es.L: Y he aquí, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} estaba de pie sobre ella, y dijo: «Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Abraham tu padre y el Dios de Isaac. La tierra sobre la que estás acostado te la daré a ti y a tu descendencia.
es.B: Allí, por encima de ella, estaba {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que le dijo: «Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de tu padre Abraham y de Isaac. A ti y a tus descendientes les daré el suelo sobre el que estás acostado.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} estaba de pie en lo alto de la escalera. Le dijo: «Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de tu abuelo Abraham y el Dios de tu padre Isaac. A ti y a tus descendientes les voy a dar esta tierra donde estás acostado.

fr.L: Et voici, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} se tenait au-dessus de lui, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Abraham ton père et le Dieu d’Isaac. La terre sur laquelle tu es couché, je te la donnerai, à toi et à ta descendance.
fr.B: Au-dessus se tenait {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu de ton père Abraham et d’Isaac. Ce sol où tu es couché, je vous le donnerai, à toi et à tes descendants.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} se tenait en haut de l’escalier. Il a dit : « Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu de ton grand-père Abraham et le Dieu de ton père Isaac. Je vais te donner cette terre où tu es couché, à toi et à tes descendants.

sw.L: Na tazama, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa amesimama juu yake, akasema, "Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Abrahamu baba yako, na Mungu wa Isaka. Nchi hii unayoilalia, nitakupa wewe na uzao wako.
sw.B: Hapo juu yake alisimama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akasema, "Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa baba yako Abrahamu na wa Isaka. Nitakupa wewe na wazao wako ardhi hii unayoilalia.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa amesimama juu ya ngazi. Akasema, "Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa babu yako Abrahamu na Mungu wa baba yako Isaka. Nitakupa wewe na wazao wako nchi hii unayolala juu yake.

decisions.choice: stood above it: above the stairway
decisions.reason: The Hebrew (nitsav alav) can mean "above it", the stairway, or "over him" or "beside him", Jacob. The LORD stands at the top of the stairway, or beside the sleeping Jacob. Either way, God himself speaks to Jacob.

decisions.choice: Abraham your father: your forefather
decisions.reason: Abraham was Jacob's grandfather; "father" is often used for an ancestor.

decisions.choice: the land ... I will give: the promise to Abraham renewed
decisions.reason: God repeats to Jacob the promises of land, offspring and blessing given to Abraham (12:7; 13:15-16) and Isaac (26:3-4).

decisions.choice: he said (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: "He" refers to the LORD, so it takes the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: your grandfather Abraham ... your father Isaac
decisions.reason: Readable makes the relationships plain (m2).

decisions.choice: "au-dessus de lui"
decisions.reason: "Lui" can refer to the stairway ("escalier" is masculine) or to Jacob, so French Literal keeps the double reading the meaning decision describes.

source.text: וְהָיָ֤ה זַרְעֲךָ֙ כַּעֲפַ֣ר הָאָ֔רֶץ וּפָרַצְתָּ֛ יָ֥מָּה וָקֵ֖דְמָה וְצָפֹ֣נָה וָנֶ֑גְבָּה וְנִבְרֲכ֥וּ בְךָ֛ כָּל־מִשְׁפְּחֹ֥ת הָאֲדָמָ֖ה וּבְזַרְעֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will be your offspring like [the] dust of the earth, and you will spread out to [the] west and to [the] east and to [the] north and to [the] south; and will be blessed in you all [the] families of the ground, and in your offspring.

en.L: And your offspring shall be like the dust of the earth, and you shall spread out to the west and to the east and to the north and to the south; and in you and in your offspring all the families of the earth shall be blessed.
en.B: Your descendants will be as countless as the dust of the earth, and you will burst out westward and eastward, northward and southward. Through you and your descendants, all the families of the earth will receive blessing.
en.R: You will have as many descendants as there are specks of dust on the earth. They will spread out in every direction: west, east, north and south. Through you and your descendants all the families on earth will be blessed.

es.L: Y tu descendencia será como el polvo de la tierra, y te abrirás paso hacia el occidente y hacia el oriente, hacia el norte y hacia el sur; y en ti y en tu descendencia serán bendecidas todas las familias de la tierra.
es.B: Tus descendientes serán tan incontables como el polvo de la tierra, y te expandirás hacia el oeste y el este, hacia el norte y el sur. Por medio de ti y de tus descendientes recibirán bendición todas las familias de la tierra.
es.R: Vas a tener tantos descendientes como granos de polvo hay en la tierra. Se extenderán por todas partes: al oeste, al este, al norte y al sur. Por medio de ti y de tus descendientes, todas las familias de la tierra serán bendecidas.

fr.L: Et ta descendance sera comme la poussière de la terre, et tu déborderas vers l’ouest et vers l’est, vers le nord et vers le sud ; et en toi et en ta descendance seront bénies toutes les familles de la terre.
fr.B: Tes descendants seront aussi innombrables que la poussière de la terre, et tu te déploieras vers l’ouest et vers l’est, vers le nord et vers le sud. Par toi et par tes descendants, toutes les familles de la terre recevront la bénédiction.
fr.R: Tu auras autant de descendants qu’il y a de grains de poussière sur la terre. Ils s’étendront dans toutes les directions : à l’ouest, à l’est, au nord et au sud. Grâce à toi et à tes descendants, toutes les familles de la terre seront bénies.

sw.L: Na uzao wako utakuwa kama vumbi la ardhi, nawe utafurika kuelekea magharibi na mashariki, kaskazini na kusini; na kupitia wewe na kupitia uzao wako, koo zote za dunia zitabarikiwa.
sw.B: Wazao wako watakuwa wengi wasiohesabika kama vumbi la ardhi, nawe utaenea kwa nguvu magharibi na mashariki, kaskazini na kusini. Kupitia wewe na wazao wako, jamaa zote za dunia zitapata baraka.
sw.R: Utakuwa na wazao wengi kama chembe za vumbi duniani. Wataenea pande zote: magharibi, mashariki, kaskazini na kusini. Kupitia wewe na wazao wako, jamaa zote duniani zitabarikiwa.

decisions.choice: like the dust of the earth: as God promised Abraham
decisions.reason: God told Abraham his offspring would be as many as the dust (13:16). Abraham had been told to look out over the land in every direction (13:14).

decisions.choice: spread out (parats): break out, burst through
decisions.reason: The verb means to break out beyond limits. It is used of Jacob's flocks increasing (30:30, 43) and is the root of the name Perez (38:29).

decisions.choice: in you ... all the families of the earth shall be blessed: the promise of 12:3
decisions.reason: The same words, "all the families of the earth", were spoken to Abraham (12:3). The verb form here (nivrekhu) is the one used in 12:3 and 18:18. The promise reaches its goal in the gospel going to all nations (Galatians 3:8).

decisions.choice: "tu déborderas" (L), "tu te déploieras" (B)
decisions.reason: Parats means to break out beyond limits (m2); "déborder" keeps the picture of overflowing at Literal.

source.text: וְהִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י עִמָּ֗ךְ וּשְׁמַרְתִּ֨יךָ֙ בְּכֹ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־תֵּלֵ֔ךְ וַהֲשִׁ֣בֹתִ֔יךָ אֶל־הָאֲדָמָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את כִּ֚י לֹ֣א אֶֽעֱזָבְךָ֔ עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִם־עָשִׂ֔יתִי אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And look, I [am] with you, and I will keep you in all [the places] where you go, and I will bring you back to this land; for not I will leave you until that I have done what I have spoken to you.

en.L: And look, I am with you and will keep you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land; for I will not leave you until I have done what I have spoken to you."
en.B: I am with you. I will guard you everywhere you go and bring you back to this land. I will not abandon you before I have done all I told you I would do."
en.R: I am with you. I will protect you everywhere you go. And I will bring you back to this land. I will stay with you until I have done everything I promised you."

es.L: Y he aquí, yo estoy contigo y te protegeré en todo lugar adonde vayas, y te traeré de vuelta a esta tierra; pues no te abandonaré hasta que haya cumplido lo que te he hablado».
es.B: Yo estoy contigo. Te cuidaré dondequiera que vayas y te traeré de vuelta a esta tierra. No te abandonaré antes de haber hecho todo lo que te he dicho que haría».

decisions.choice: I am with you: God goes with the fugitive
decisions.reason: Jacob is leaving the land alone and in danger. God promises his presence, protection and return, the things Jacob then asks for in his vow (verses 20-21). God repeats "I will be with you" when he sends Jacob home (31:3).

decisions.choice: keep (shamar): watch over, protect
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in the priestly blessing, "the LORD bless you and keep you" (Numbers 6:24), and in Psalm 121, which speaks of the LORD watching over a traveler.

decisions.choice: I will stay with you until
alternatives: I will not leave you until
decisions.reason: Readable states the negative promise positively.

source.text: וַיִּיקַ֣ץ יַעֲקֹב֮ מִשְּׁנָתוֹ֒ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אָכֵן֙ יֵ֣שׁ יְהוָ֔ה בַּמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וְאָנֹכִ֖י לֹ֥א יָדָֽעְתִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: And awoke Jacob from his sleep and said, surely there is YHWH in this place, and I, not I knew [it].

en.L: And Jacob awoke from his sleep and said, "Surely {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is in this place, and I did not know it."
en.B: When Jacob woke from sleep, he said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is truly here in this place, and I had no idea!"
en.R: Then Jacob woke up. He said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is really here in this place! But I did not know it."

es.L: Y despertó Jacob de su sueño y dijo: «De veras {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está en este lugar, y yo, yo no lo sabía».
es.B: Cuando Jacob despertó, dijo: «¡{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está realmente aquí, en este lugar, y yo ni me había dado cuenta!».
es.R: Entonces Jacob se despertó. Dijo: «¡{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está de verdad en este lugar! Pero yo no lo sabía».

fr.L: Et Jacob s’éveilla de son sommeil et dit : « Vraiment, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est en ce lieu, et moi, je ne le savais pas. »
fr.B: Quand Jacob sortit de son sommeil, il dit : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vraiment ici, en ce lieu, et je n’en savais rien ! »
fr.R: Ensuite Jacob s’est réveillé. Il a dit : « {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vraiment ici, à cet endroit ! Mais je ne le savais pas. »

sw.L: Ndipo Yakobo akaamka usingizini, akasema, "Kweli {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} yuko mahali hapa, na mimi, mimi sikutambua."
sw.B: Yakobo alipoamka kutoka usingizini, akasema, "Kumbe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} yuko hapa kweli, mahali hapa, nami sikujua kabisa!"
sw.R: Kisha Yakobo akaamka. Akasema, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} yuko hapa kweli! Lakini mimi sikujua."

decisions.choice: surely the LORD is in this place: God present where he was not expected
decisions.reason: Jacob had stopped at a place by chance, far from his father's altars (26:25). He learns that God was there before him.

decisions.choice: and I, I did not know it: Jacob stresses himself
decisions.reason: The pronoun "I" is stated, which Hebrew does not need. Jacob, the one who knew how to plan and scheme, did not know this.

source.text: וַיִּירָא֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר מַה־נּוֹרָ֖א הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה אֵ֣ין זֶ֗ה כִּ֚י אִם־בֵּ֣ית אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְזֶ֖ה שַׁ֥עַר הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he was afraid and said, how awesome [is] this place! This [is] nothing other than [the] house of God, and this [is the] gate of the heavens.

en.L: And he was afraid and said, "How awesome is this place! This is nothing other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven."
en.B: He was filled with fear and said, "What a fearsome place this is! This is God's own house, and here is the doorway into heaven."
en.R: Jacob was afraid. He said, "This place is holy and frightening! It must be God's house. This is the gate to heaven."

es.L: Y tuvo miedo y dijo: «¡Cuán temible es este lugar! Esto no es otra cosa que la casa de Dios, y esta es la puerta de los cielos».
es.B: Lleno de temor, dijo: «¡Qué lugar tan imponente es este! Es la casa misma de Dios, y aquí está la entrada al cielo».
es.R: Jacob tuvo miedo. Dijo: «¡Este lugar es santo y da miedo! Tiene que ser la casa de Dios. Esta es la puerta del cielo».

fr.L: Et il eut peur et dit : « Combien ce lieu est redoutable ! Ce n’est rien d’autre que la maison de Dieu, et c’est ici la porte des cieux. »
fr.B: Saisi de crainte, il dit : « Qu’il est impressionnant, ce lieu ! C’est la maison même de Dieu, et voici la porte qui ouvre sur le ciel. »
fr.R: Jacob a eu peur. Il a dit : « Cet endroit est saint, il fait trembler ! Ce doit être la maison de Dieu. C’est la porte du ciel. »

sw.L: Akaingiwa na hofu, akasema, "Jinsi gani mahali hapa palivyo pa kutisha! Hii si kitu kingine ila nyumba ya Mungu, na hili ni lango la mbingu."
sw.B: Akajawa na hofu, akasema, "Mahali hapa ni pa kuogofya mno! Hii ni nyumba ya Mungu mwenyewe, na huu ni mlango wa kuingia mbinguni."
sw.R: Yakobo akaogopa. Akasema, "Mahali hapa ni patakatifu na pa kutisha! Lazima hii ni nyumba ya Mungu. Huu ni mlango wa mbinguni."

decisions.choice: afraid ... awesome: holy fear
decisions.reason: Both words come from the same root (yare). Jacob's fear is awe in the presence of God, as when people meet God elsewhere (Exodus 3:6).

decisions.choice: the house of God (beit elohim): God's dwelling place
decisions.reason: Jacob names what the place is; in verse 19 he gives it the name Bethel, "house of God".

decisions.choice: the gate of heaven: the true entrance to God
decisions.reason: In the ancient Near East a temple was thought of as a meeting point of heaven and earth. Babylon's name was understood as "gate of god". The people of Babel tried to build a tower reaching to heaven (11:4); here God himself opens the way.

source.text: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם יַעֲקֹ֜ב בַּבֹּ֗קֶר וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֶת־הָאֶ֨בֶן֙ אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֣ם מְרַֽאֲשֹׁתָ֔יו וַיָּ֥שֶׂם אֹתָ֖הּ מַצֵּבָ֑ה וַיִּצֹ֥ק שֶׁ֖מֶן עַל־רֹאשָֽׁהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And rose early Jacob in the morning and took the stone that he had put [at] his head, and he set it up [as] a pillar, and poured oil on its top.

en.L: And Jacob rose early in the morning and took the stone that he had put at his head, and set it up as a pillar, and poured oil on top of it.
en.B: Early the next morning Jacob took the stone he had placed by his head, stood it upright as a sacred pillar, and poured oil over its top.
en.R: Early in the morning Jacob took the stone he had put by his head. He stood it up on its end as a pillar to mark the place. Then he poured oil on top of it.

es.L: Y se levantó Jacob temprano por la mañana y tomó la piedra que había puesto junto a su cabeza, y la erigió como pilar, y derramó aceite sobre su cima.
es.B: A la mañana siguiente, muy temprano, Jacob tomó la piedra que había colocado junto a su cabeza, la puso en pie como pilar sagrado y derramó aceite sobre ella.

fr.L: Et Jacob se leva tôt le matin, et il prit la pierre qu’il avait mise à son chevet, et il la dressa en stèle, et il versa de l’huile sur son sommet.
fr.B: Le lendemain, de bon matin, Jacob prit la pierre qu’il avait placée près de sa tête, la dressa comme une stèle sacrée et répandit de l’huile sur son sommet.
fr.R: Tôt le matin, Jacob a pris la pierre qu’il avait mise près de sa tête. Il l’a dressée debout comme un pilier, pour marquer l’endroit. Puis il a versé de l’huile dessus.

sw.L: Naye Yakobo akaamka mapema asubuhi, akalichukua lile jiwe alilokuwa ameliweka penye kichwa chake, akalisimika kuwa nguzo, akamwaga mafuta kileleni pake.

sw.R: Asubuhi na mapema Yakobo alichukua jiwe lile alilokuwa ameliweka karibu na kichwa chake. Akalisimamisha wima kama nguzo ya kuonyesha mahali pale. Kisha akamimina mafuta juu yake.

decisions.choice: a pillar (matsevah): a standing stone marking a holy place
decisions.reason: A standing stone was set up to remember an event or to mark a place of worship (31:45; 35:14). Later the Law forbade such pillars because they had become part of Canaanite worship (Deuteronomy 16:22), but here it is Jacob's memorial of God's appearing.

decisions.choice: poured oil: setting the stone apart for God
decisions.reason: Pouring oil on something dedicated it to God, as priests and the tabernacle were later anointed (Exodus 30:26-30). Jacob does the same again at Bethel when he returns (35:14).

decisions.choice: "une stèle" (L, B); "un pilier" (R)
decisions.reason: "Stèle" is the usual French word for a standing stone set up as a memorial (m1); Readable uses the plainer "pilier", as the English says "pillar".

en.B: He named that place Bethel, though the town had been called Luz before.
en.R: Jacob named that place Bethel, which means "house of God." Before that, the town was called Luz.

sw.L: Naye akapaita mahali pale jina lake Betheli; lakini jina la mji hapo kwanza lilikuwa Luzu.

sw.R: Yakobo akapaita mahali pale Betheli, maana yake "nyumba ya Mungu." Kabla ya hapo, mji huo uliitwa Luzu.

decisions.choice: Bethel: "house of God"
decisions.reason: The name repeats what Jacob said in verse 17. Bethel became one of the best-known holy places of Israel (35:1-15; 1 Samuel 7:16), later a center of false worship (1 Kings 12:28-29).

decisions.choice: Luz: the earlier name of the town
decisions.reason: Luz may mean "almond tree". The story explains how the place came to be known as Bethel (35:6; Judges 1:23).

decisions.choice: which means "house of God"
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the name.

decisions.choice: vowed a vow: a solemn promise to God
decisions.reason: A vow was a promise to God, often made in need and kept when God answered (Numbers 21:2; 1 Samuel 1:11). It was binding and must be paid (Deuteronomy 23:21). Jacob is reminded of this vow on his return (31:13; 35:1-3).

decisions.choice: if God will be with me: taking God at his word
decisions.reason: Jacob's conditions repeat what God has just promised (verse 15): to be with him, keep him and bring him back. The "if" can be heard as doubt or as "since"; either way Jacob builds his vow on God's promise.

decisions.choice: made a solemn promise to God
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a vow is (m1).

decisions.choice: then the LORD shall be my God: the beginning of the promise
alternatives: and if the LORD will be my God, then (verse 22)
decisions.reason: The "if" part may end with "in peace to my father's house", so that Jacob promises to take the LORD as his God; or it may run on, "and the LORD will be my God", so that the promise begins in verse 22. The Hebrew allows both. Either way the vow turns on the LORD being Jacob's God, where before he spoke of "your God" to his father (27:20).

decisions.choice: in peace (beshalom): safe and well
decisions.reason: Shalom here means safety and wholeness. God brings Jacob back "safely" (shalem) to Shechem (33:18).

decisions.choice: then
decisions.reason: The word "then" marks where this translation takes the promise to begin (m1).

decisions.choice: this stone shall be God's house: a place of worship
decisions.reason: The pillar will mark a sanctuary where God is worshiped. Jacob later builds an altar here (35:7).

decisions.choice: I will surely give a tenth: a tithe
decisions.reason: Abraham gave Melchizedek a tenth of the spoil (14:20). A tenth of produce was later given to God by law (Leviticus 27:30). The doubled verb (aser a'asserennu) makes it emphatic.

decisions.choice: you give me ... to you: Jacob turns to speak to God
decisions.reason: Jacob began by speaking of God (verse 20); at the end he speaks to him directly.

decisions.choice: you (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: Jacob speaks to God, so "you" takes the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: no deity pronoun span
decisions.reason: Swahili marks "you" inside the verbs ("utakachonipa", "nitakurudishia"), where no capital is possible, and adding a free "wewe" would only be there to carry the setting.
